weakness: The program only pushed the box along one axis (away from the robot) and relied on dragging it sideways with a finger in contact to fix any error along the other axis; with the box starting 0.3 m from the catch point along that other axis, the box never got past the boundary line (0/10).
how_found: Listed where the pipeline assumes objects start: the approach and push targets were computed at the box's own x and only the y error was ever re-checked, which only works if the box already starts near the landing x as in the default spawn.
why_missed: Every default seed spawns the box within 4 cm of the landing x, so a one-axis push plus friction drag passed the base task; the first draft was shaped by the default spawn rather than by the goal geometry.
fix: Measure the box's offset from the target on both axes and, when the x offset exceeds 2.5 cm, first push the box along x with one fingertip on its x face (calibrated 5.7 cm contact offset, 6 cm segments at about 0.3 m/s), back off, then do the y push as before.
general_rule: Plan a push from the full vector between where the object is and where it must go, pushing along each needed direction from the appropriate face, instead of assuming the object starts where it usually does.

weakness: The program always put the hand 15 cm behind the object in a fixed grip, never looked for other things on the table and planned no collision checks against them; a fixed block 11-14 cm behind the box sat exactly where the trailing finger had to go, so the hand jammed against it, the push never started and the episodes stalled (0/10, six seeds hit the 15 min worker timeout).
how_found: Questioned what is between the gripper and the target: the approach and push poses were computed only from the box pose, with no obstacle query and no avoid list, and the chosen grip needs a large empty strip behind the object.
why_missed: The default scene has nothing on the table but the task objects, so the free space the grip needed was never visible as a requirement; the grip was tuned for contact geometry only.
fix: Query get_obstacles() at the start; compute the free strip each grip needs behind the object and switch from the 'fingers along the push' grip (needs ~22 cm) to a 'fingers across, hand offset 6 cm to the side' grip (needs ~9 cm) when the first is blocked; pass the obstacles as avoid on free-space moves and descend straight into the narrow slot. While repairing, the base task exposed a second weakness: the first push went all the way to an early, noisy landing estimate and the late re-prediction loop was skipped when the early release-time estimate was too soon; now the first push stops at the lane centre, release time is floored at 5.3 s, and corrections creep forward in 5 cm steps until 0.45 s before release.
general_rule: Before choosing how to hold a tool or approach an object, check the free space that grasp or approach actually needs against everything perceived nearby, and keep an alternative grip with a smaller footprint for cluttered cases.

weakness: Once the box had been pushed into place the program only kept re-checking the one coordinate it was correcting (y) and could only push from the robot side; when the box was knocked 7 cm sideways two seconds before the catch it never noticed the new x error, and its fixed sequence of special-case manoeuvres (push x once, then y, an expensive go-round only for -y) could neither re-plan nor fit the remaining time (2/10).
how_found: Questioned whether objects move after the robot has acted on them: the correction loop compared only dy against the target and assumed the box stays where the last push left it.
why_missed: In the default scene nothing touches the box except the gripper, so a one-axis correction loop after an open-loop placement always looked sufficient; disturbances after placement were never imagined.
fix: Replaced the scripted push sequence with a closed-loop controller: every cycle it re-predicts the landing, measures the box on both axes, picks the axis to fix (x first), moves the hand over the top of the box to the right face only when needed and only if the remaining time allows, pushes, and if the box stopped short of where the hand pushed it learns that shortfall and pushes further next time. Six repair iterations: one-axis re-check (0.2), faster re-centring (0.4, 0.4), conservative early y target plus side-step push-back (0.3), general face-switching controller (0.7), learned push overshoot (0.8).
general_rule: After acting on an object, keep re-measuring every quantity the success condition depends on until the deadline, and correct with a general closed loop that can choose any approach direction, rather than a fixed script that only re-checks what it last changed.

weakness: When the box was shoved 7 cm away from the robot 1.1-2.3 s before the catch, the program could only undo it by moving the hand over the box to its far side and pushing back; that manoeuvre took 1.2-1.8 s (a 90 degree wrist turn alone cost ~0.5 s, the far side was out of reach for the default grip, and the hand had to stay out of the ball's flight corridor), so it finished after the ball left the ramp on most seeds (best 0.4 over five repairs; v3 also dropped to 0.4-0.7 while trying).
how_found: Questioned the assumption, kept after round 3, that late corrections are cheap because the hand already rests on the robot-side face; a disturbance in the other direction close to the deadline tests whether the controller can reverse in time.
why_missed: The default scene never moves the box away from the hand, and the round-3 fix was tuned on a sideways knock that a side push could undo; reversal time near the deadline was never budgeted.
fix: Tried, not kept (dev/pipeline_v4_last_attempt.py): face-dependent grips with the compact grip for the far face, reach fallback, keep-out of the flight corridor, earlier stop near the exit, home-orientation grip by default to avoid wrist turns, longer push segments. None reached 0.8 on v4 without breaking v3. Pipeline reverted to the round-3 version; v4 marked unsolved.
general_rule: Budget the worst-case time to reverse a correction against the deadline before committing to a one-sided strategy; if reversing takes longer than the time left, constrain the object on both sides (or hold it) rather than relying on pushing from one side.

weakness: The program treated every perceived obstacle as a full-height wall and always pushed with the fingertips 6 mm above the table; a 2.2 cm rail 3-9 cm behind the box made both grips look blocked, the fingers came down on the rail and the push never started (2/10).
how_found: Questioned what lies under the hand rather than beside it: the push height was a constant and the free-space check ignored obstacle heights, while the contact only needs the fingertips somewhere on the 4 cm box wall.
why_missed: The table was empty in every earlier scene, and the round-2 obstacle was taller than the hand, so height never mattered; the push height was tuned once for the bare table.
fix: Average the noisy obstacle boxes over 10 looks, raise the push height just enough for the fingertips to clear low obstacles near the box (as long as they still meet the box wall below its rim), and ignore those obstacles in the free-space check. Keeping v3 at 0.8 needed a second change: each push now closes the loop on the box itself (extra short slides while the box is still short and still moving), because a box turned by a bump presents a corner and the fixed contact offset left it 2-5 cm short.
general_rule: Use the measured heights of nearby objects, not just their footprints, to pick the contact height of a push or grasp within the band the target allows, and close the loop on the object's position rather than on the hand's.
